clues.title: Bells mistaken for fire
clues.claim: Wyat reported hearing a bell, assuming there was a fire, and following soldiers toward King Street.
clues.question: Q1
clues.locator: Deposition, opening: Hearing a bell ring
clues.speaker: William Wyat
clues.uncertainty: His reported initial assumption does not establish why the bells rang.

clues.title: An officer’s command
clues.claim: Wyat reported that an officer repeatedly ordered the soldiers to fire before the first shot.
clues.question: Q2
clues.speaker: William Wyat
clues.uncertainty: A disputed report; identifying a voice and identifying its speaker are separate problems.

clues.title: Prince heard no order
clues.claim: Prince reported hearing no order to fire; he described Preston coming out from behind the soldiers.
clues.question: Q2
clues.speaker: Newton Prince
clues.uncertainty: Failure to hear an order cannot prove that nobody gave one. NPS summarizes Preston as in front.

clues.title: A different man
clues.claim: Jane Whitehouse, identified by MHS as Jane Crothers, said the man encouraging the soldiers to fire was not Captain Preston.
clues.question: Q2
clues.locator: PDF p. 2, Jane Whitehouse paragraph; MHS Jane Crothers section
clues.speaker: Jane Crothers / Whitehouse
clues.uncertainty: She excluded Preston but did not name the man; the scene does not supply an identity.

clues.title: Palmes and the first shot
clues.claim: Palmes said something resembling snow or ice struck a soldier immediately before the first shot; he then heard an unidentified voice say fire.
clues.question: Q1
clues.speaker: Richard Palmes
clues.uncertainty: He did not identify who spoke; his description is not proof of a coordinated order.

clues.title: Bliss described blows
clues.claim: Theodore Bliss reported snowballs and a stick striking a soldier before the firing.
clues.question: Q1
clues.speaker: Theodore Bliss
clues.uncertainty: This account describes some actions, not the conduct of every person in the crowd.

clues.title: Leaving toward the west
clues.claim: Prince said he was moving west of the soldiers when he heard the guns and saw the dead carried away.
clues.question: Q1
clues.speaker: Newton Prince
clues.uncertainty: A moving observer’s view and hearing need not match another witness’s.

clues.title: Four printed coffins
clues.claim: The March 12 Boston Gazette account was accompanied by four coffin images.
clues.question: Q3
clues.speaker: Edes and Gill; imagery attributed to Revere
clues.uncertainty: Verified through the Library of Congress description, not a local original issue scan.

clues.title: Clothing and identification
clues.claim: Whitehouse described the unidentified man in dark clothes and said he did not look like an officer.
clues.question: Q2
clues.speaker: Jane Crothers / Whitehouse
clues.uncertainty: Appearance is her reported impression, not a secure identification.

clues.title: A town committee’s selection
clues.claim: MHS identifies 96 depositions collected for the Boston town committee’s Short Narrative.
clues.question: Q3
clues.locator: A Short Narrative of the Horrid Massacre, 1770 section
clues.speaker: Boston town committee
clues.uncertainty: The compilation and individual depositions are not independent corroborating witnesses.

clues.title: A competing London account
clues.claim: The Fair Account used testimonies gathered by British officers and sent to England; MHS identifies 31 testimonies in that collection.
clues.question: Q3
clues.locator: A Fair Account of the Late Unhappy Disturbance at Boston, 1770 section
clues.speaker: British officers; Francis Maseres
clues.uncertainty: Do not confuse this 31-item collection with the separate 26-deposition subset discussed in later scholarship. Boston arrival date is unverified.

clues.title: The image makes an argument
clues.claim: Revere’s engraving labels the Custom House Butcher’s Hall, a visual accusation rather than a neutral building label.
clues.question: Q3
clues.speaker: Paul Revere, after Henry Pelham
clues.uncertainty: An engraving is a composed representation, not a photograph or proof of the precise firing formation.

clues.title: Verdicts did not settle every detail
clues.claim: Preston was acquitted in October; the soldiers’ trial ended with six acquittals and two manslaughter convictions.
clues.question: Q2
clues.locator: The Trial of Captain Preston; The Trial of the Soldiers
clues.speaker: Trial juries; NPS summary
clues.uncertainty: An acquittal is a legal result, not proof that every disputed observation has been resolved.

witnesses.name: William Wyat
witnesses.description: A speaker represented through his March deposition.
witnesses.knowledge: Only C01 and C02; do not add biography or assert a proven commander identity.
witnesses.greeting: I can tell you what I reported hearing that night.

witnesses.name: Newton Prince
witnesses.description: A witness represented through his recorded trial account.
witnesses.knowledge: Only C03 and C07; distinguish not hearing from proof of silence.
witnesses.greeting: My account begins with what I could see and hear near the soldiers.

witnesses.name: Jane Crothers
witnesses.description: Recorded at trial as Jane Whitehouse; identification connected by MHS.
witnesses.knowledge: Only C04 and C09. Do not invent the unknown man’s identity. Marriage is not grounds to dismiss her testimony.
witnesses.greeting: I described a man, but I could not give his name.

witnesses.name: Print-shop apprentice
witnesses.description: A fictional facilitator for verified documents, not a historical eyewitness.
witnesses.knowledge: Discuss the five verified document cards only. Archival cards are modern interventions; do not claim personal delivery or observation.
witnesses.greeting: The same event can look different on another printed page. Examine these accounts.

comparisons.title: Hearing a command — or hearing none
comparisons.text: Wyat reported a command; Prince reported hearing none. Position, timing and identification limit the comparison. Neither entry proves dishonesty.

comparisons.title: Who was the speaker?
comparisons.text: Wyat described an officer; Crothers/Whitehouse excluded Preston. Do the accounts identify the same voice or moment?

comparisons.title: Two published collections
comparisons.text: The Boston committee and British officers assembled different collections. Their institutional framing matters; repeating a deposition does not create a new witness.

comparisons.title: An image and a report of violence
comparisons.text: Compare Bliss’s description of objects striking soldiers with the engraving’s accusatory composition. The print communicates an argument rather than recording every action.

comparisons.title: Position and observation
comparisons.text: A historical plan can help ask where a witness stood. It cannot recover every moving observer’s exact view.
